Backlog visibility through the end of the decade reduces execution risk amid a choppy tape.

RTX offers diversified exposure across Raytheon missiles/air defense (Patriot, LTAMDS), Pratt & Whitney engines, and Collins Aerospace, with the GTF powder-metal overhang now largely priced in. Bullish options and institutional flows plus a relatively resilient 1M performance (-1.0%) suggest smart money is rotating into primes as missile replenishment orders accelerate. Entry under $180 looks attractive given the long-cycle backlog.

Diversifies the defense exposure beyond primes into high-growth tactical tech.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Here's what's interesting: the smart money is quietly rotating into the classic "early cycle recovery" trade — Real Estate, Materials, and Tech are getting loaded up on, which usually happens when big players think rate cuts are coming and infrastructure/reshoring money is about to flow. Materials in particular at 3x normal volume lines up with the tariff regime and the push to rebuild domestic supply chains for things like steel, copper, and rare earths; Tech bullishness despite stretched valuations tells me funds are betting the AI capex boom and any deregulation push (looser antitrust, lighter AI rules) keeps the party going. On the flip side, the bearish bets on Consumer Discretionary, Staples, Industrials, and Financials are screaming recession-hedge — when options traders pay up to protect BOTH Discretionary (high-end spending) AND Staples (toothpaste and soup), they're telling you they expect the consumer to crack regardless of income level, likely because tariff pass-through is about to hit shelf prices while student loan payments, credit card delinquencies, and a cooling job market squeeze wallets. The credit market confirms it — junk bonds (HYG) getting hammered with puts while investment-grade (LQD) gets bought is textbook "flight to quality," meaning the pros think weaker companies are about to struggle refinancing, which is why Financials are getting sold (loan losses coming) and Energy too (demand destruction in a slowdown). The contradiction worth flagging: indexes near highs while this defensive positioning builds underneath is the kind of divergence that precedes a 5-10% correction in the next 4-8 weeks, not a crash but a real gut-check.
